_comment: Where this template's mechanisms came FROM, and how far each source has been read. Written by hand, read by bin/skeletor-maintain, never merged from. skeletor was extracted from a mature production repository and that repository kept going; this is the record of how far along it we have looked. An upstream is located by its origin URL, never by a path — a path is right on one machine and wrong on every other.

jam-sense.why: the repository every mechanism in this template was extracted from

sources.cli/task.py: the second capture intake, and the argument for two lanes over a --kind flag
sources.scripts/reporting/remediation.py: the Capture descriptor: one engine, N lanes, and drainer_line deriving a schedule from the job registry rather than storing it
sources.scripts/reporting/bug_capture.py: the shared capture engine this template's cli/_capture.py is a smaller version of
sources.tests/test_pyright_scope.py: the caller scan: config pins OR every caller passes --pythonpath. Merged to develop as 8835dff73 (PR #1423). It is also the one file here whose direction has reversed: jam-sense took it FROM this template at v0.4.2 (their .skeletor-components.json records it at the path it had then, template/python/tests/test_pyright_scope.py), added the interpreter half, and it came back. Expect it to keep moving in both directions rather than reading either way as drift.
sources..claude/rules/commits.md: the commit-type rule, harvested 2026-09-08 from e6e14d8cf: `docs:` is decided by whether a human wrote prose for a human, never by whether the file sits under docs/. A path predicate pushes README.md, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md edits into `chore:`, and it had already been violated here — this repository's own log carried `docs(readme):` against a root file while docs/rules/commits.md said docs/ only. Watch it: this is a rule both trees state in prose and neither enforces, so it drifts silently in both.
sources..vscode/settings.json: the issue and pull-request query grouping — the read side of the capture lanes. Ours are generated from scripts/lanes.py; theirs were hand-maintained. GRADUATED from sources_untracked on 2026-09-08: 9be786e96 tracked it upstream (`.vscode/*` plus a re-include, since git cannot re-include through an excluded directory), so it now has a history a watermark can measure and is watchable from here for the first time.

sources_untracked._comment: Harvested from, and NOT trackable: gitignored upstream, so no history for a watermark to measure against and this report can never say whether they moved. Recorded as a limit rather than rediscovered as an error on every run — and kept out of `sources`, because a path git cannot see is not the same fact as one that has left the tree. EMPTY since 2026-09-08, when its one entry graduated: jam-sense tracked .vscode/settings.json in 9be786e96, crediting the skeletor session that noticed it. The category stays because the limit is real and the next harvest from an ignored path needs somewhere honest to sit — but note which way this resolved. The limit was reported here for a fortnight as permanent, and it was closed by the upstream changing, not by a better instrument. An untrackable source is a fact about the other repository's .gitignore, so telling them is a remedy and this file had treated it purely as something to endure.

_not_taken._comment: Judged and declined, with the reason, so the next pass does not re-litigate it. An entry here is a decision; delete it if the reason stops holding rather than silently harvesting anyway.

jam-sense.scripts/reporting/remediation.py (the dr: 2501 lines of Kuma monitors, an escalation policy and a run ledger. The template ships ONE fully-worked job on purpose — a registry seeded with keys whose modules do not exist is red on arrival — so the drain side stays the adopter's. The capture side ported; the drain side is named by scripts/lanes.py and left to them.
jam-sense.scripts/reporting/agent_test_gap.py: a lane with no producer in this template. A view whose label nothing can create is empty forever, and an empty pane and a drained queue render identically.
jam-sense.the editor fallback on a capture (jam ta: worth having and not yet ported. It needs a body template per lane, which is a second copy of Lane.sections unless it is generated from them.
jam-sense.the agent-fix / agent-fix-excluded parki: labels nothing in this template applies. Same rule as the test-gap lane: a lane needs a producer, and a view whose label nothing can create is empty forever — indistinguishable from a queue you have kept clear.
jam-sense.a gate asserting the pinned virtualenv E: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-08, and the correction is the useful part. This was declined as 'correct and unassertable', which was true of the instrument being used and false of the question: `venvPath` is relative to the config file, so whether it resolves is a fact about the CHECKOUT, which no unit test can hold — red in CI, red in an unprovisioned worktree, neither a defect. But bin/skeletor-verify BUILT the checkout, so it is the one caller entitled to ask, and pyright_pin() now asserts the pin resolves to the interpreter the grid built. The decline had generalised 'the tree cannot assert this' to 'nobody can', which is this workspace's own unit-of-observation rule read one step too far. The limit stays written into pyrightconfig.json for the adopter, where it is still true.
jam-sense.scripts/lint_pyright_gate.py (the pre-fl: Worth having and NOT yet ported — a real gap, recorded so the next pass does not have to re-derive it. It resolves the interpreter pyright will actually use, proves it can import a sentinel package, and refuses to run pyright at all when the probe fails, on the grounds that 94 diagnostics naming the wrong thing are worse than none. This template has the same exposure for the same reason: reportMissingImports is `none`, so a bare interpreter degrades every project name to Unknown and the fallout lands in files the commit never touched. Not taken now because it is a new script plus a rewiring of the pyright hook plus its own tests, and because the generator-side half of the problem — does the pin resolve at all — was closed first and is where this grid could see it. The adopter-side half is still open.
jam-sense.scripts/docs/regen_indexes.py format_mar: Does not apply. Their bug was a generator invoked directly skipping the prettier re-flow that the wrapper applied on the way out, so a no-op run rewrote 1086 lines. This template's scripts/docs/ generators never format, so the direct route and the `docs regen` route emit identical bytes and Invariant 4 (a regeneration that changed nothing produces no diff) holds by construction. Re-check if a formatting step is ever added to one route only.
jam-sense.cli/report._records_this_run (7319ec947,: Cannot occur here. Their funnel keyed the run ledger on `job.key if job else module`, so two hand-written commands that are deliberately absent from the registry wrote rows under their module name and three consumers each drew a wrong conclusion. This template GENERATES every report subcommand from the registry and _run_module does a hard JOBS_BY_KEY[job_key] lookup, so a non-job has no route into the funnel. Re-check if a hand-written report subcommand is ever added alongside the generated ones — that is the exact precondition.
